theory_title: What the fine print charges you for
theory_content: Compare four things rather than the advertised interest rate: the minimum balance requirement and the penalty for breaching it, free ATM withdrawals per month, debit card annual fees, and charges for cheque returns. A "zero balance" account with ₹500 in hidden annual fees costs more than a ₹10,000 minimum balance account without them.

theory_title: Automating the parts you should not have to decide
theory_content: Standing instructions for SIPs, EMIs and insurance premiums remove the two ways people fail: forgetting, and deciding not to this month. Set them for the day after payday, not the end of the month, so the money leaves before it can be spent. Keep a small buffer in the account, because a bounced auto-debit costs a fee and a mark on your credit record.

theory_title: What happens to the balance afterwards
theory_content: A joint account with "either or survivor" passes directly to the survivor without paperwork. A single account without a nominee requires a succession certificate — months of court process at the worst possible time. Adding a nominee takes ten minutes online and is the single highest-value piece of financial admin most people have never done.

theory_title: Small habits that remove most of the risk
theory_content: Set a low daily UPI limit and raise it deliberately when needed. Use a separate account with a small balance for online payments. Turn off international usage on cards you do not use abroad. None of these prevent a determined attack, but they cap what any single compromise can cost you, which is the realistic goal.
